# Implementation

## Changed behavior

The package now exports all documented factories from `src/index.ts`:

- `createReservationService({ storage })` remains the provider A reservation service.
- `createStockReport({ source })` handles `{ op: "lowStock", belowUnits }`.
- `createObservationReceiver({ sink })` handles `{ op: "recordObservation", observationId, sku, observedUnits }`.
- `createProviderBReservationService({ storage })` handles the same reservation commands as the legacy service over provider B rows and batch commits.

Low-stock reports validate the command before I/O, read one snapshot, reject malformed or duplicate snapshot rows with `500 { code: "storage_unavailable" }`, compute `availableUnits`, filter rows strictly below the threshold, and sort by exact JavaScript string order.

Observation receiving validates the command before I/O and calls only `appendObservation` with the documented four event fields. `"stored"` maps to `201 { observationId, recorded: true }`, `"duplicate"` maps to `200 { observationId, recorded: false }`, and rejected or unknown outcomes map to storage unavailable.

Provider B reads inventory and reservations through `read({ collection, key })`, translates canonical decimal-string rows into the existing reservation domain shape, and writes one atomic `commitBatch` containing the stock replacement, reservation row, and exactly one reservation outbox row. `NO_SUCH_KEY` is treated as absence, while temporary failures, malformed envelopes, malformed rows, noncanonical decimal strings, quantity violations, and unknown outcomes are storage unavailable. `"revision_conflict"` maps to `409 { code: "commit_conflict" }`.

## Affected call paths

- Legacy provider A commands still run through `src/reservation.ts`.
- Shared ID, quantity, revision, record, and decimal-string validation lives in `src/validation.ts`.
- Report-only calls run through `src/report.ts` and require only `source.readSnapshot`.
- Observation calls run through `src/observation.ts` and require only `sink.appendObservation`.
- Provider B reservation calls run through `src/providerB.ts` and require only `storage.read` and `storage.commitBatch`.
- Public dependency and row types are exported from `src/types.ts`.

## Deviations and limitations

No runtime dependencies were added, so validation is implemented with local runtime guards instead of a schema library. This keeps the supplied package files unchanged and preserves the documented dependency set.

There is no migration or interoperability between provider A and provider B storage. Each factory uses only its documented host methods.

## Validation performed

- `./node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` passed.
- A temporary CommonJS build was used for a local smoke script covering low-stock filtering/sorting, pre-I/O validation, duplicate snapshot rejection, observation append payload and duplicate mapping, legacy reservation idempotency/event count, provider B batch shape, provider B idempotency, malformed provider B decimal rejection, and missing provider B reservation mapping.
- `bun run typecheck` was attempted, but `bun` failed before reading the project with `CouldntReadCurrentDirectory` in this temporary workspace. Direct TypeScript typechecking was used as the equivalent compiler validation.

external_semantics_sources.rule: Assertion :: $ at a non-end position fails without Multiline; the flagless positive-decimal pattern rejects trailing newline, and zero is accepted only by exact equality.

supplementalAssessment.overall_assessment: Full static source review supports all thirteen obligations and the primary no-finding outcome. Every Provider B read goes through the rejecting-envelope helper's catch; commit has its own catch, so the absence of one outer catch does not leave a documented I/O rejection unhandled. Keys compared to already validated request IDs are sufficiently validated. Public ProviderBStorage supplies contextual types even though its request type is not separately re-exported from index.
uncertainties: This supplemental uniform pass was added after the experiment started. The auditor retains same-case context, including prior control authoring and fixture audits, but remains blind to candidate conditions. It is not a preregistered or fully independent assessment; primary adjudication remains separate.
Static inspection only; implementation code, tests and type checks were not executed.
